text:
jon: ran an nsys snapshot on the TRT-vllm integration, attaching raw snippet. seeing an odd skew: wrapper syncs + CPU-side scheduler take ~62% of total.
maya: can you paste the nsys summary? rough numbers are fine.
jon: paste below:\n```
Time(%)  Calls  Avg(ms)  Name
62.1     1      42.3     wrapper::synchronize_and_schedule
20.4    256      1.2     tensorrt::engine_invoke
10.0   1024      0.2     cudaMemcpyAsync (KV warmup)
5.5    512       0.05    kernel::softmax
2.0    512       0.01    other kernels
```
sophia: whoa 42ms single call for wrapper sync is huge. is that wallclock inside a mutex/condition wait? any stack traces?
jon: attached perfetto flame slice shows the wrapper blocked on `scheduler::pop_batch` and then a `std::condition_variable::wait` back to the scheduler thread. looks like scheduling spin + context switch when batches are tiny.
alex: what's our batch size distribution? I bet we're getting lots of size=1/2 because the heuristic mispredicts peak throughput and we bail early.
jon: exactly. logs: most requests terminate early due to latency SLO path. sample: `batcher.emit(size=1, timeout=1ms)`. jitter in arrival causes small batches.
maya: kv cache memcopies at 10% suggest cold-cache warmup is expensive. are we copying whole KV per invocation rather than streaming?
jon: current wrapper copies KV for every engine instance on invocation path to keep URL-addressable caches isolated. we profiled: memcpy ~0.15ms per KV shard; multiplies across heads and layers.
sophia: quick ideas: 1) make KV sharing lock-free/read-copy-update so wrapper don't copy; 2) let scheduler aggregate small inflight requests for up to X ms; 3) move KV memcpy off the critical path (cudaMemcpyAsync + stream pri).
alex: agreed. also consider moving `tensorrt::engine_invoke` to a dedicated pool so wrapper thread doesn't block on engine queueing; let it push to GPU queue and return fast.
perf-bot: perf regression alert: ctx#3345 shows wrapper sync median increased 3.8x vs baseline-2026-02. Regression correlated with scheduler change revert_eb62.
jon: noted. I rolled a minimal repro to a dev box: `nsys profile --output=tmp/nsys_trt --trace=cuda,cublas --capture-range=nvtx --profile-child-processes ./serve_local` ; results in attached tev.
maya: can you run with cuda-memcheck and `nsys nvtx` markers around batcher/scheduler boundaries so we get clearer slices?
jon: will do. Also trying a microtrace with perfetto to capture the CPU wakeups (syscalls) between wrapper and scheduler.
sophia: for quick win we can raise the batch timeout from 1ms->6ms for requests tagged low-latency and see throughput change. worth A/B test.
alex: also experiment with `cudaStreamAttachMemAsync` (if available) and pinned host buffers to reduce memcpy jitter.
jon: plan: (1) instrument NVTX around pop/push in scheduler (2) run nsys+perfetto with pinned buffers and async memcopy (3) try RW lock for KV + benchmark memcopy removed path (4) telemetry: add histogram metric for batch sizes and wrapper wait time.
maya: I can help implement the NVTX hooks and batching histogram.
sophia: I'll prototype RW lock path for KV sharing. if safe, we can gate behind a feature flag.
ci-bot: build #trt-vllm-integration passed on PR 5123 (nvtx-instrumentation). staging deployment queued.
jon: thanks. I'll post back with updated nsys snapshot. closing loop: main suspects = scheduler heuristics causing small batches, wrapper-level KV copies on critical path, and a regression introduced by scheduler change revert_eb62. action items above.
maya: :thumbsup:
alex: +1\n
